summary: Fixed the RSS feed parser bug in courier/fetcher.py (replaced response.json() with RDF/RSS 1.0 XML parsing) and implemented the full run_pipeline() orchestration with fetch→filter→process→compile→summary pipeline, per-article atomic status writes, retry/permanent-skip logic, article cap, dry-run mode, and run summary output.

specLite.problemStatement: run_pipeline() was a placeholder stub with no pipeline logic; additionally fetcher.py called response.json() on an RDF/RSS 1.0 XML feed, which raises a parse error on any real run.
requirements: Fix courier/fetcher.py: replace response.json() with RDF/RSS 1.0 XML parsing returning list[dict] with keys url, title, timestamp
Filter out articles in COMPILED, PERMANENTLY_SKIPPED, UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT_TYPE states; cap at config.max_articles_per_run
Track per-article fetch failures; permanently skip after config.max_fetch_attempts
Atomic status writes via store.write_status() after each article is processed
Print run summary to stdout: compiled count, failed, skipped, output path
dry_run=True prints the article list and exits without writing anything; since_days accepted but not yet filtered (# TODO: US-002)
specLite.architecturalNotes: The orchestrator is the top-level coordinator in a strict single-responsibility pipeline. It calls fetcher.fetch_feed() → fetcher.fetch_article() → extractor.extract_article() → compiler.compile_document(), delegating all side effects to existing modules. store.py handles status reads/writes with atomic rename. No new architectural patterns introduced.
